omission_flags: Omits existing pre-loss defensive measures (MCMC website blocks, SC Investor Alert Lists, banking kill switches), creating a falsely absolute picture that the state only acts after a loss.

cardinal_sin_flags.quote: why every defence the state runs activates only after the money has already left.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: Absolute statement contradicted by SC Investor Alert List, MCMC website blocking, NSRC kill switches which activate before/during the transaction.
cardinal_sin_flags.fix: Change to 'why the strongest state responses primarily activate after the money has already left' or 'why law enforcement only activates after the loss'.

cardinal_sin_flags.quote: with no power over the wiring that keeps catching.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: MCMC has authority to block websites and a mandatory social-media licensing framework. State lacks ability to make platforms financially liable, distinct from 'no power'.
cardinal_sin_flags.fix: Change to 'with no mechanism to hold the wiring financially liable when it catches.'

cardinal_sin_flags.quote: The Securities Commission's enforcement records held about 111 unregulated entities and 26 cease-and-desist orders by mid-2025
cardinal_sin_flags.why: Could not independently verify these specific mid-year tallies.
cardinal_sin_flags.fix: Soften to 'dozens of unregulated entities and multiple cease-and-desist orders'.

overall_assessment: Pivots away from victim-blaming toward systemic vulnerability, citing verified CCID data. Rhetorical strength leads to factual overreaches: 'every defence' ignores pre-loss interventions; the 111/26 SC tallies could not be verified. Strip absolute language and soften unverified tallies.
